untrained_description: When my other cat was a kitten, he was obsessed with twist ties and hair ties and I would shoot them across the room for him to chase. He grew out of chasing the hair ties when we introduced a new kitten, Bellies (the cat who plays fetch). We noticed she liked the twist ties too and one day we flicked a hair tie (elastic) across the room and she chased it down and brought it right back. She fetched those hair ties for about a day or two but then stopped fetching them for a month or more so I thought it was a fluke. For awhile, she would only fetch them sporadically but after about a year, we realized it's pretty consistent. She will even fetch them when she has to climb stairs or jump over things. Sometimes she'll bring it back but about 3-4 feet from where you are. However, we just discovered she's caught on to that a bit and if no one has thrown her hair tie within 10 minutes or so, she'll pick it up and bring it closer to you. We learned that for her to bring it back, we have to be careful not to distract her, make any eye contact, or call her name because she'll get distracted/excited and forgets what she's doing.
object_three: probably anything light and bouncy that she could carry in her mouth
extra_comments: Lately, Bellies has been following us to bed with her hair tie in tow so we can get a few final games in. She's been known to wake me up in the morning by plopping her hair tie in my face. She's really quite impressive with her determination to find the hair tie. Sometimes I accidentally flick them between the couch and the wall but somehow she manages to find it. She's gotten one that got stuck on the top of the shower curtain, on a shelf that she definitely shouldn't have been on, one that got tossed under a pile of laundry — she'll even find one that's downstairs and bring it back up the stairs.

untrained_description: Toulouse had outgrown his kitten collar and it was just sitting around the house. He would pick it up and play with it, which could get pretty annoying as it had a little bell on it. I think one time he played with it hard enough that it got me, so I picked it up and threw it across the room. Toulouse just hopped up and chased it, played with it across the room for a bit, and then picked it up in his mouth and brought it back. So I threw it again. Toulouse taught himself how to fetch.
extra_comments: We’ve sort of weened Toulouse off fetching when we started using hair ties as the fetching item of choice for him. We would lose the hair ties under furniture, and Toulouse would steal the hair ties we use for our hair out of their spots in hopes of having us play with him. We stopped playing fetch with him to preserve our hair tie stock. Also I have a friend who used hair ties for fetching with their kitten (Mocha), and Mocha ate one of the hair ties and gave my friend and her boyfriend a scare; so I figure it’s probably for the best that Toulouse stops putting hair ties in his mouth.

She's very particular about what she'll fetch, however. She'll smack anything around, but if you want to play fetch it HAS to be this one type of cosmetic swab. (It's like a Q-tip, but much thinner. Used for eyelash extensions. Tulip is interested in regular Q-tips, but she won't fetch them).

untrained_description: Bam was very attached to a specific object (an old cotton makeup pad that we called her “fluffy”). I expected her to go and get it for herself, but after doing that she brought it back and dropped it at my feet. This happened regularly from this point on.
extra_comments:
Bam would also get very distressed if she wasn’t able to find her “fluffy”, which would often lead to us finding it outside the laundry window. How or why she was dropping it out the window is a mystery.
At a certain age, possibly coinciding with moving house and having children, Bam stopped playing fetch and ended up losing her fluffy for good. She also just became less playful in general at this point.

Green mouse is one of her oldest toys (we've had it about 18 months) and she plays with it the most--usually batting it around the room and chasing it, sometimes she picks it up in her mouth and carries it somewhere else, sometimes she sort of hides it and then pounces on it. She has another toy that is identical to green mouse except that it is purple and she doesn't play with it quite as much.

His younger brother, Junior, who is less friendly (they were both feral but Junior was considerably older when I got him and did not socialize as well) has copied this behavior precisely once, bringing me a toy while I was sitting on the couch. Junior sometimes runs after the toys with Soot when I throw them, but usually doesn't retrieve them/lets Soot have them. Mostly he prefers to play this game with mouse toys or similarly sized toys. untrained_description:

Originally we would throw a toy and expect him to just enjoy chasing it across the house, but he figured out that if he brought it back he could get us to throw it again so he could keep chasing it. untrained_description: I received Zelda at about 3-4mo old from a friend. After she had acclimated to her new home she immediately began demonstrating fetching behavior. Upon throwing a toy she played with it for a moment before trotting back carrying the toy in her mouth, often loudly meowing while carrying it, and would come to sit on the ground about 1-3ft away from you. If you approached she dropped the toy. If you threw the toy the behavior would repeat. She only displays this behavior with her favorite toys
object_one: Kick toy composed of 4 cloth balls on a string. This was the toy she was first given at the shelter when she was born.
object_two: Little mice toys. Must be made of hollow cardboard and wrapped in fabric for her to care about them.
object_three: Small puff ball toys, like the pompoms of a knitted hat.
object_preferred: Little mice toys. Must be made of hollow cardboard and wrapped in fabric for her to care about them.
extra_comments: The only thing limiting her fetching behavior is me. She could play fetch all day, every day if I facilitated it. She has multiple ways of initiating. First she'll bring the toy she wants to fetch with to me quietly, either by carrying and dropping it 1-3ft away or by batting it across the room to your feet, and wait for you to throw it. Second, she won't bring the toy to me, but carry it in her mouth and meow loudly to announce she wants to play fetch and get me to come to her. If you ignore her she gets more insistent up to the point of dropping the toy directly on top of you, especially while lying down in bed. I will sometimes wake up sleeping on top of her fetch toys in the morning because she wanted to play at some point in the night while I was thoroughly unconscious. She won't initiate fetch while I'm at my work desk (I work from home). She only initiates while I'm walking around the apartment or after my workday, I'm assuming because she knows when her chances of goading me into playing fetch are the highest.
